title: YESTERDAY HE WAS A PRISONER.
paragraphs:
Chains on his wrists.
Dust on his skin.
Two years forgotten in a dungeon.
He stands before the throne of Egypt.

The guards who once shoved him into darkness now escort him into a palace blazing with gold.
Torches flicker against towering pillars.
Perfumed air replaces the smell of stone and rot.

Not a guard.
Not a servant.
But Joseph is still a Hebrew slave.
And Pharaoh has a problem no empire can solve.

Seven fat cows rise from the Nile—healthy, powerful.
Then seven skeletal cows emerge… and devour them.

Seven full heads of grain.
Then seven thin, blighted heads swallow them whole.
Egypt’s magicians stare at the floor.
Then a servant whispers a name.
“You’ve heard my dreams can be interpreted,” the king says.
Joseph could have seized the moment.
He could have said, “Yes, I have the gift.”
But Joseph does something dangerous in a room full of power.

“I cannot do it,” Joseph says.
“But God will give Pharaoh the answer he desires.”
— Genesis 41:16

Seven years of overflowing abundance are coming.
Fields bursting.
Barns overflowing.
So severe the years of plenty will be forgotten.
History itself will bend under hunger.

“Store grain during the years of abundance.
Prepare before the famine arrives.”
The king turns to his court.

“Can we find anyone like this man—
one in whom is the Spirit of God?”

Pharaoh removes his signet ring.
Places it on Joseph’s hand.

Fine linen replaces prison rags.
A gold chain rests on his chest.
And the cry echoes through Egypt:
Second ruler of the most powerful empire on earth.
But this story is bigger than promotion.

Joseph’s pit.
Joseph’s slavery.
Joseph’s prison.
Every dark hallway led to this throne room moment.
Because God was not just raising Joseph.
He was positioning him to save nations.
And centuries later, another innocent man would stand before a ruler.
And through that cross, He saved not just nations—
Maybe today feels like Joseph’s prison.

But the God who lifted Joseph in a single day
is the same God who writes your story.
Your dungeon is not your destiny.
God is preparing something bigger than you can see.
Doors open that no prison can hold shut.
Because someone you know is sitting in a prison season right now.
And they need to hear this truth:
“We tell the stories that shame tried to erase.”
